data.name: Rose
data.gender_notes: Rose is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Rose is a name derived from the Hebrew word 'Rosh', which means 'head'. It can also be linked to the Greek and Latin words 'Ros', meaning 'dew of the rose' and 'rose flower' respectively.
data.long_meaning: The name Rose has a rich history in Christianity, rooted in both the Old and New Testaments. In the Old Testament, the name Rose is associated with the Hebrew word 'Rosh', which means 'head'. This name is also linked to the Greek and Latin words 'Ros', meaning 'dew of the rose' and 'rose flower' respectively. In the New Testament, the name Rose is symbolic of the resurrection of Christ, as a rose blooms after winter's end, and represents the Virgin Mary and her purity. Additionally, the name Rose is associated with the martyr Rose of Limos, who was believed to have a rose bush grow up around her grave.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Rose symbolizes new beginnings, resurrection, and the beauty of the Virgin Mary.
data.etymology: Rose belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rose is a name derived from the Hebrew word 'Rosh', which means 'head'. data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rose total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: ורד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ורד מקורו בערבית ומשמעותו פרח הורד, שמסמל לאהבה, יופי ונצחון. ביהדות, הורד הוא סמל לאהבה ולתשוקה, והוא מוזכר בספר הזוהר. השם ורד הוא גם שם של צמח הורד, שידוע בפריחתו היפה ובריחתו הנעים.

in_greek.name: Ρόδη
in_greek.meaning: Άνθος ρόδου, σύμβολο αγάπης και νίκης
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ρόδη προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη ρόδη, που σημαίνει άνθος ρόδου. Ο ρόδον είναι σύμβολο αγάπης, ομορφιάς και νίκης στην ελληνική μυθολογία. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο όνομα Ρόδη, αλλά το ρόδον αναφέρεται ως σύμβολο αγάπης και τρυφής.

historical_references.reference: In the Middle Ages, roses were often used as symbols of the Virgin Mary. Rose gardens were planted near monasteries and convents. The rose was also associated with the Passion of Christ, as the Five Wounds of Christ were likened to the five petals of the rose.

During the Renaissance, roses were used in art and literature as symbols of love and beauty. In this context, the name Rose became a popular given name for girls, as a sign of the beauty and grace of the Virgin Mary and the ideal of Christian womanhood.
